newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish steady to lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended steady to lower, with the long end under profit-taking pressure heading into the weekend, traders said.
Trading was choppy and indecisive much of the day, wandering between a nine-month high and support at 114-25/32.
Traders said some players may have decided to take profts heading into the weekend amid the idea the market's rally this week may have been overdone.
"We've had a good strong run (but) we're starting to have less impulse to the upside," said Eric Herndon, vice president taxable trading for Griffin, Kubik, Stephens and Thompson.
Traders said technical factors took center stage and many technicians cast wary eyes to resistance above 115-00.

"Over the course of the last two days that market has done real well and we got up to these resistance levels with no dramatic fundamental news, so people are now taking profits," said Kurt Fraim, futures analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston.
"You get to these levels and people start thinking it might be time for a pullback," he said. "Or on the other hand, they wonder if we're going to go through it and force people to buy it," he said.
Other technicians pegged a barrier above the market from 115-15/32 to 115-24/32.
In light of that resistance and this week's mixed bag of economic data, bullish momentum waned, traders said.
"Fundamentally, we need to hear continuously that the economy is slowing further than we think it is now and some of the things we've gotten don't back up that view," Griffin's Herndon said.
"I think we pushed it a little too far, too fast," Herndon said of the rally to nine-month highs. "Yes, the economy is a little slower, but not that slow," he said.
December T-bond options and T-note options expired at midday with little fanfare.
Dec T-bonds settled down 11/32 to 114-30/32, muni-bonds fell 12/32 to 117-1/32, March Euros were flat at 94.49 and Dec 10-year notes lost 5/32 to 110-22/32.
